statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail holds the low edge of the watch band because the overnight NQ path retraced in both directions, while Stress stays high on a 5.24% 10-year yield, crude near 93 and a wide semiconductor dispersion.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state stays WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A narrow elevated-risk window is flagged from 13:30 to 15:00 UTC, spanning the US cash open and the 14:00 UTC JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence releases, where the published forecast maps to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES for one hour. Outside that window the published forecast returns to the watch and low bands.
headline: Overnight NQ fully retraces both a dip to 30,372.25 and a push to 30,635.25 while the 10-year yield holds a 19-year high at 5.24%
body:
NQ front-month trades near 30,565 against a 30,566.25 prior close, effectively unchanged on the session after an overnight range of 30,372.25-30,635.25. That 0.86% band was travelled in both directions: the early dip toward 30,372.25 and the subsequent push to a fresh overnight high at 30,635.25 were each fully retraced, which is the central reason Tail stays at the low edge of the watch band rather than stepping into the elevated band. ES futures are 7,740.50, down 0.08%, inside a 7,716.00-7,754.25 range. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Monday at 30,276.81, down 1.08%, roughly 200 points above its 30,081.06 session low. VIX is unchanged at 16.07 within a 15.98-16.19 range, an implied-volatility reading that actively conflicts with the macro backdrop and argues against a pathological price path being priced.

The macro regime itself remains genuinely difficult, which is what keeps Stress in the high band. The 10-year Treasury yield sits at 5.24-5.25%, its highest since 2007, the 30-year is near 5.56% and the 2-year advanced roughly 8 basis points to about 4.93% on Monday. Market pricing for an October Federal Reserve rate increase is roughly 70-78%. WTI crude is 92.83, up 0.25%, having faded from a 94.74 overnight high, with Brent in the 105-106 area after Monday's move above 107 when the Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz was rejected. The energy impulse is therefore two-sided rather than escalating at the assessment cutoff.

Index internals stay the main source of dispersion. Monday's session produced a semiconductor drawdown on AI-safety headlines, with the PHLX Semiconductor Index down about 2%, ARM -8.7%, Qualcomm -7.2%, Intel -5.7%, AMD -3.6% and Micron -2.6%, while Nvidia gained 1.7% on a 150 billion dollar buyback authorisation. Megacaps split the same way: Meta -4.8% and Tesla -3.9% against Nvidia's gain. Wide dispersion of this kind usually raises Stress and lowers directional conviction rather than establishing the persistent one-way path that Tail measures.

Shared Finviz context was read at the start of this run. Its collection timestamp of 07:33:03Z is about two hours old, beyond the 90-minute freshness threshold, its collectionStatus is partial, and its futures and calendar sections are unavailable. It was therefore used only as stale latest-session corroboration of the breadth, megacap and semiconductor picture, and all current levels above come from independently verified primary sources.

A narrow elevated-risk window is flagged from 13:30 to 15:00 UTC, covering the US cash open and the 14:00 UTC JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence cluster. That stacking of an opening auction with high-impact labour and sentiment data is the one part of the published forecast where Tail is modelled into the elevated band. Outside that window the forecast returns to the watch band and decays into the low band overnight.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hours were published. Tail ranged from 17 to 27. Only two single-hour excursions reached the elevated band, at 09:00 and 14:00 UTC on Monday, and each reverted within the following hour. Tail troughed at 17 through the late Monday and early Tuesday overnight session, then oscillated between 20 and 24 from 01:00 UTC as the European handover approached, printing 20 in each of the last three hours. Stress never fell below 76 and peaked at 85 at 10:00 UTC on Monday, reflecting the persistent high-yield and high-oil regime rather than any single release. Confidence held between 85 and 88 throughout. The dominant mode alternated between trend-down during the Monday cash session and early Tuesday European hours, normal through the quiet overnight window, and mixed once two-way structure re-established itself.
outlookSummary: The published forecast keeps Tail in the watch band through the European and early US session, with a single elevated-band hour at 14:00 UTC where JOLTS Job Openings, JOLTS Job Quits and CB Consumer Confidence print 30 minutes into the cash session. That stacking of the opening auction with high-impact releases is the only flagged hour, and Tail is modelled to decay back into the watch band by 15:00 UTC on an orderly price-discovery assumption. Overnight hours into Wednesday return to the low band before Tail steps back to the watch band from 04:00 UTC as the European handover and quarter-end approach. The final hours of the horizon carry a further step as positioning builds into the Wednesday ADP, final Q2 GDP, Core PCE and Chicago PMI cluster. Confidence decays monotonically across the horizon because the evidence base ages, not because a specific input is missing.
